scoring_justification: Exponent and ratio are recomputed from the agent's raw temperature series; room-temperature K_lat and ZA contribution are compared to paper gold with tolerance to accommodate DFT code differences.

hidden_assets.purpose: Reference values for K_lat(300K), exponent α, ratio bounds, ZA contribution
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Paper-reported: K_lat=645 W/mK at 300 K (Section 3.2, Fig.2b); fitted exponent 0.735 (Section 3.2); K_RTA ≈ half of K_lat at 300 K (Section 3.2, Fig.2b); ZA contribution ~60% (Section 3.4, Fig.4d).
hidden_assets.generation_method: Extracted directly from the paper text and figures.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: These are the paper's own quantitative results for the same quantities, same units, same conditions.

schema.description: Temperature series with iterative and RTA lattice thermal conductivity.

outputs.description: Temperature-dependent lattice thermal conductivity; the checker recomputes the power‑law exponent from the series, compares K_lat at 300 K to a hidden reference, and verifies that K_RTA is roughly half of K_lat at 300 K.

schema.description: Phonon branch contributions to K_lat at 300 K.

outputs.description: Phonon branch contributions at 300 K; the checker verifies that the ZA contribution is within tolerance of the paper‑reported value.

output_contract.notes: The two CSV files are the only scored artifacts. The process steps (harmonic IFCs, anharmonic IFCs) are mandatory to produce the necessary input for ShengBTE but are not directly scored. The checker recomputes the thermal conductivity exponent and ratio, and checks the ZA contribution; all comparisons use tolerances appropriate for DFT‑code differences.

steps.description: K_lat at 300 K compared to paper value 645 W/mK with tolerance ±50 W/mK; partial credit outside tolerance.
Power-law exponent α from log-log fit of K_lat vs T; compared to 0.735 with tolerance ±0.05.
K_RTA / K_lat at 300 K must lie between 0.4 and 0.6 (penalised outside).
ZA branch contribution to total K_lat at 300 K compared to 60% with tolerance ±5 percentage points.
